text: My belief is that, like any domain or industry, the more it matters, the more the design matters.
speaker: Karri Saarinen
context: Lenny asks Karri about when design can be enough of a differentiator against incumbents and whether founders should invest heavily in design versus other areas like distribution or technology. Karri explains his theory about how design becomes increasingly important as markets mature and become more crowded. He argues that in new paradigms like mobile or web, early products don't need great design since they're first to market, but as competition increases, the design bar rises significantly.
text_ko: 제 생각에는 다른 어떤 분야나 산업과 마찬가지로, 중요할수록 디자인이 더 큰 차이를 만들어요.
text_zh: 我觉得，和任何行业一样，越重要的事，设计就越关键。
text_es: Creo que, como en cualquier sector, cuanto más importante es algo, más crítico resulta el diseño.
key_sentence: The more it matters, the more design matters; the bar is so high.
original_text: My belief is that, like any domain or industry, the more it matters, the more the design matters. What happens is whenever there's a new paradigm, I don't know, like the mobile or the web or something the first iterations of those products existing there, they don't have to be super well designed necessarily because they are the first. Then, as you build the 100,000 different email clients, any email client now has to be pretty good to be even considered an email client. It's like the bar is so high.

vocabulary.definition: Design refers to the process of creating a plan or convention for the construction of an object or system, encompassing aesthetics, functionality, and user experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, design is crucial for product development, branding, and user interface, as it directly impacts customer satisfaction and market success.
vocabulary.nuance: While design often emphasizes visual aspects, it also encompasses strategic thinking about usability and user engagement, making it a multifaceted concept.

text: I think today it's almost a very basic thing now. Pretty much from the very beginning, you need pretty high level design for people to even pay attention or consider you seriously.
speaker: Karri Saarinen
context: Karri continues explaining why design has become crucial for modern startups. He points out that unlike older companies like Google or YouTube that launched with very basic websites, today's startups need high-quality design from day one just to get noticed. He acknowledges this creates an unfair barrier where good products might be dismissed simply due to poor visual design, even when the underlying functionality is solid.
text_ko: 요즘엔 이게 거의 기본이에요. 처음부터 사람들의 관심을 끌고 진지하게 고려되려면 꽤 높은 수준의 디자인(high-level design)이 필요해요.
text_zh: 我觉得现在这几乎成了基本门槛。一开始就得有相当高水准的设计(design)，别人才能注意你、把你当回事。
text_es: Hoy en día eso ya es casi algo básico: prácticamente desde el principio necesitas un diseño de alto nivel (high-level design) para que la gente siquiera te preste atención o te tome en serio.
key_sentence: High level design is necessary to pay attention and consider you seriously.
original_text: I think today it's almost a very basic thing now. Pretty much from the very beginning, you need pretty high level design for people to even pay attention or consider you seriously. And I think it's not necessarily fair because sometimes it's like maybe the product is really good but they didn't have a designer or they didn't have time to do it and then people just dismiss it because it doesn't seem like something that they interest them.

vocabulary.definition: To think carefully about something, typically before making a decision.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, 'consider' is often used when evaluating options, strategies, or proposals before taking action.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a thoughtful and deliberate process, often implying that multiple factors are being weighed.

vocabulary.definition: An abstract representation of a system or product that outlines its architecture and components without delving into detailed implementation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup settings, 'high level design' is crucial for communicating the overall vision and structure of a project to stakeholders and team members.
vocabulary.nuance: This term emphasizes the strategic overview rather than technical specifics, making it suitable for discussions with non-technical stakeholders.

vocabulary.definition: To focus one's mind on something; to give careful consideration or notice to a particular matter.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'pay attention' often refers to the need for stakeholders, employees, or customers to be aware of important information or changes that could impact their decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase can imply a call to action, suggesting that the subject matter is significant enough to warrant focused observation.

text: So I think similarly, with startups or SaaS, it's like your landing page or some of the other things.
speaker: Karri Saarinen
context: Karri draws an analogy between product packaging (like Apple's attention to unboxing experiences) and startup design elements like landing pages. He explains that design serves as the first impression that sets user expectations before they even try the product. This is particularly valuable for unknown startups that need to establish credibility and quality perception from the first interaction, making design a powerful form of leverage in the early stages.
text_ko: 저도 비슷하게 생각해요. 스타트업(startups)이나 SaaS(SaaS) 쪽에서는 랜딩 페이지(landing page)나 그런 다른 요소들이 중요한 편이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得对初创公司(startups)或软件即服务(SaaS)来说也是这样，像你的落地页(landing page)或其他一些环节就很关键。
text_es: Creo que con las startups o con el software como servicio (SaaS) pasa algo parecido: tu página de aterrizaje (landing page) y otras cosas.
key_sentence: it's like your landing page or some of the other things.
original_text: So I think similarly, with startups or SaaS, it's like your landing page or some of the other things. It's like they are already communicating something to the user and they're setting the expectations and then I think that that can be very useful thing, especially early on when no one really knows you or knows the product or cares about you. So I think especially, I feel like design can be very good leverage in the beginning.

text: So for every project there's a project lead. That lead can be engineer or designer. It's not a formal role or it's not based on your whatever level or it's just like you need to be certain title that you can be that.
speaker: Karri Saarinen
context: Lenny asks how Linear functions with only one product manager across the entire company. Karri explains their project-based leadership model where engineers and designers take turns being project leads. This isn't a formal hierarchy based on seniority or titles, but rather a rotating assignment system where someone takes responsibility for driving a specific project forward, coordinating with the team, and managing communications about progress.
text_ko: 프로젝트마다 프로젝트 리드(project lead)가 있어요. 그 리드는 엔지니어(engineer)일 수도 있고 디자이너(designer)일 수도 있어요. 정식 직책이나 경력 레벨에 따라 정해지는 건 아니고, 특정 타이틀이 있어야만 맡을 수 있는 역할도 아니에요.
text_zh: 每个项目都会有个项目负责人(project lead)，可以是工程师也可以是设计师。这不是一个正式的职位，也不是按你的级别或头衔来定的，没必要非得有某个特定头衔才能担任。
text_es: Así que para cada proyecto hay un responsable del proyecto (project lead). Ese responsable puede ser un ingeniero o un diseñador. No es un rol formal ni depende de tu nivel ni de tener un título concreto para poder serlo.
key_sentence: That lead can be engineer or designer.
original_text: So for every project there's a project lead. That lead can be engineer or designer. It's not a formal role or it's not based on your whatever level or it's just like you need to be certain title that you can be that. It's more like an assignment that now you are responsible getting the project started and working together with the team, figuring it out, and then communicating changes or communicating how that progress happens.

vocabulary.definition: A project lead is an individual responsible for overseeing and guiding a specific project from inception to completion, ensuring that objectives are met and resources are utilized effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, the project lead coordinates team efforts, manages timelines, and communicates with stakeholders to ensure project success.
vocabulary.nuance: While the title of project lead may not always be formalized, it implies a level of authority and accountability that is crucial for project execution.

vocabulary.definition: A formal role refers to an officially recognized position within an organization, typically defined by specific responsibilities and authority.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate structures, formal roles delineate job functions, helping to establish clear lines of responsibility and accountability among employees.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'formal role' suggests a level of hierarchy and structure, which may not always apply in more fluid or collaborative work environments.

vocabulary.definition: An engineer or designer refers to professionals who apply technical and creative skills to develop products, systems, or solutions, often collaborating closely in project settings.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and design firms, engineers and designers play critical roles in the development process, contributing their expertise to ensure that projects are both functional and aesthetically pleasing.
vocabulary.nuance: The phrase suggests a collaborative relationship between technical and creative disciplines, highlighting the importance of both perspectives in successful project outcomes.

text: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me.
speaker: Karri Saarinen
context: Lenny asks about Linear's approach of not using metrics-based goals or A/B testing, which differs from many other companies. Karri explains his philosophy that over-reliance on data often stems from fear of making wrong decisions. He argues that leaders should make decisions based on customer understanding and intuition rather than letting data make choices for them, emphasizing the importance of taking ownership of decisions rather than hiding behind metrics.
text_ko: 사람들이 가끔 데이터를(data)를 많이, 심지어 과하게 쓰는 건 '내가 잘못된 선택을 할까?' 하는 불안이나 두려움 때문이라고 생각해요. 그래서 스스로 선택하기보다 데이터를 통해 선택을 대신하게끔 하는 거예요.
text_zh: 我觉得有时候人们会把数据用得很多、甚至过头了，因为害怕会做错决定，就让数据替自己做主。
text_es: Creo que a veces la gente se apoya demasiado en los datos (data) porque tiene miedo de equivocarse: se preguntan "¿voy a tomar la decisión equivocada?" y acaban dejando que los datos decidan por ellos.
key_sentence: people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice?
original_text: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me. But then you might still feel like this is not the right choice, but the data is telling me is the right choice and then turns out maybe it was the right choice or not. But at least we made that choice and the data didn't make that choice for us.

vocabulary.definition: To select an option or course of action that leads to an undesirable or negative outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, making the wrong choice can have significant repercussions, affecting everything from project success to financial stability.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the potential for error in decision-making, often highlighting the fear or anxiety associated with uncertainty.

text: I think there's always things that you're supposed to do or it sounds like a good idea to do. And it could be like, yeah, come to this podcast. And I actually think before it wasn't like...
speaker: Karri Saarinen
context: Lenny asks Karri about his exceptional focus and ability to avoid distractions, noting how difficult it was to get him on the podcast initially. Karri shares his decision-making framework for maintaining focus, explaining that he constantly evaluates whether activities are important to do now versus later. He uses the podcast example to illustrate how he delayed this interview until Linear reached a stage where the conversation would be more valuable and interesting.
text_ko: 늘 해야 할 것 같거나, 하면 좋을 것 같은 일들이 있는 것 같아요. 예를 들어 '이 팟캐스트에 나와보세요' 같은 제안일 수 있죠. 근데 사실 전에는 꼭 그렇게 생각하지 않았어요.
text_zh: 我觉得总有些事别人觉得你应该做，或者听起来是个好主意。比如有人会说，“来上这个播客 (podcast) 吧”。但我其实觉得以前并不是那样……
text_es: Creo que siempre hay cosas que se supone que tienes que hacer o que parecen buena idea. Puede ser algo como: “sí, ven a este pódcast (podcast)”. Y, la verdad, creo que antes no era así...
key_sentence: You're supposed to do things that sound like a good idea, but timing matters.
original_text: I think there's always things that you're supposed to do or it sounds like a good idea to do. And it could be like, yeah, come to this podcast. And I actually think before it wasn't like... Or I always have this question, is this important to do now or is it important to maybe do later? So I think, for example, the question on this podcast is I didn't feel like it was important to do it earlier because we weren't at the stage or a scale or something that I think it'd be as interesting or something.

vocabulary.definition: A suggestion or proposal that is considered beneficial or advantageous in a particular context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, identifying a 'good idea' can lead to innovative solutions, improved processes, or new product developments.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'good idea' is a positive endorsement, it can be subjective and may require further validation or analysis before implementation.
